purpose: Silence expected console.error output in two DatabaseCleanup API-failure tests via targeted jest.spyOn + mockRestore, but the PR is dominated by an unrelated 'fix composer update' commit (89ed0ff7) that deletes ~2683 tracked vendor files (~334k lines) and rewrites composer.lock.
riskRationale: The ~12-line test change is correct and verifiably passes (17/17 tests, ESLint clean), but ~99.9% of the PR diff is an out-of-scope dependency restructure: it strips the tracked PHPCS/WPCS/PHPCompatibility/PHPUnit dev toolchain from vendor/, breaks the documented `composer lint` step on any fresh checkout, leaves composer.lock mutually inconsistent with the committed vendor tree, and bumps a shipped production dependency. Four previously flagged minor test-hygiene/doc issues also persist unchanged.
breakingChanges: Tracked vendor/ dev toolchain removed (~2683 files / ~334k lines): vendor/bin/phpcs, vendor/bin/phpcbf, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, phpcompatibility, phpunit, etc. — `composer lint` fails on a fresh checkout until `composer dev-setup` is re-run
composer.lock rewritten to a dev-install state (37 packages-dev) while the committed vendor/ tree contains none of them, and production dependency symfony/css-selector bumped v7.4.8 -> v7.4.9

text: The core change achieves its goal: console.error is suppressed only in the two tests that deliberately trigger the API-failure path, all 17 DatabaseCleanup tests pass, and ESLint is clean. However, the branch is contaminated by commit 89ed0ff7 'fix composer update', which deletes ~2683 tracked vendor files and rewrites composer.lock — a massive, unrelated scope expansion that makes the diff nearly unreviewable and breaks the documented `composer lint` verification step. Four previously reported minor issues (inline mockRestore, missing spy assertions, wrong inspector.md date, duplicate reformat-only commit) also persist unfixed.

reasoning: The test-silencing change is sound, but the branch must not merge while it carries commit 89ed0ff7 (the unrelated 2683-file vendor purge and composer.lock rewrite); revert or split that commit into its own PR, and fix the inline mockRestore placement, missing spy assertions, stale inspector.md date, and duplicate commit before merge.

message: Suppression is correctly scoped to only the two tests that intentionally trigger the API-failure path (DatabaseCleanup.js:111/197), so genuine console.error output from the rest of the suite remains visible and real failures are not masked.

The pre-existing fetch-failure test is the ideal pattern to mirror — it both mutes console.error and asserts toHaveBeenCalledWith(...) — demonstrating that suppression and verification are not mutually exclusive.

The jest.spyOn(console,'error').mockImplementation(() => {}) + mockRestore() approach follows the repo's documented sad-path pattern, and the suite verifiably passes 17/17 with clean ESLint and no console.error leakage in the runner output.

Commit 89ed0ff7 'fix composer update' is a massive, unrelated scope deviation: it deletes ~2683 tracked files / ~334k lines from vendor/ — the entire dev toolchain (vendor/bin/phpcs, vendor/bin/phpcbf, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, phpcompatibility, phpcsstandards, phpunit, mockery, brain/monkey) — while composer.json still lists them as require-dev, and it rewrites composer.lock (~2364 changed lines, new content-hash, production symfony/css-selector bump v7.4.8 -> v7.4.9). This is ~99.9% of the PR diff and has nothing to do with the stated purpose of silencing console.error in a test file. It violates AGENTS.md ('vendor/ is tracked in git... git add vendor/'), breaks the documented `composer lint` step on any fresh checkout (vendor/bin/phpcs no longer exists), makes the diff effectively unreviewable, and guarantees merge conflicts with the branches that commit full vendor per repo convention.
suggestion: Revert commit 89ed0ff7 entirely so the branch contains only the test changes; if removing dev tooling from tracked vendor/ is genuinely desired, land it as its own dedicated, clearly-described PR (with composer.lock, .gitignore, and AGENTS.md updated consistently).

message: After commit 89ed0ff7, composer.lock declares ~37 dev packages (packages-dev) while the committed vendor/ tree contains none of them, so lock and vendor/ are mutually inconsistent — master's lock (6 dev packages) matched its committed vendor tree. Any later `composer install`/`update` or `git add -A` churns thousands of untracked files (the author's working tree is already dirty with a partial re-install), and `composer lint` fails for anyone who does not re-run composer dev-setup.
suggestion: Restore the consistent master state by reverting 89ed0ff7; if a real dependency change is required, regenerate lock and vendor/ together (per the composer release convention) in a separate PR.

message: consoleSpy.mockRestore() is called inline at the end of each test body (lines 235 and 271). If the waitFor assertion at line 231/267 fails, mockRestore() never executes and the console.error spy leaks into every subsequent test in the suite (jest.clearAllMocks() in beforeEach clears call history but does NOT remove the mockImplementation), silently swallowing real errors and hiding genuine failures — the opposite of this PR's goal. Previously reported and still present.
suggestion: Restore the spy in a failure-safe way, e.g. add afterEach(() => { jest.restoreAllMocks(); }) at the describe level and remove the inline consoleSpy.mockRestore() calls, or wrap the body in try/finally.

message: Both silenced tests (lines 202 and 238) mock console.error but never assert it was actually called. If the error-handling code in DatabaseCleanup.js:197 is later refactored to stop logging via console.error, these tests still pass silently and the logging regression goes unnoticed — the existing fetch-failure test at line 373 shows the correct pattern. Previously reported and still present.
suggestion: After the waitFor in each test, assert the spy fired, e.g. expect( consoleSpy ).toHaveBeenCalledWith( 'Database cleanup error:', expect.any( Error ) ) for the Error case and expect( consoleSpy ).toHaveBeenCalled() for the empty-object rejection.
